rows.text: calls the function at `00182610` + 0x8 and, when it returns non-null, calls it again (`00182610` + 0x17) and stores byte (`ecx` != 0) to byte `+0xD18` of that result; a null first result stores nothing

masks bit 0x10 out of `ecx`; when qword `0209C380` is non-null it calls the function at `0029D210` + 0x27 with it and `rdx` = 0 when the masked value is 1, else `00916330`, then the function at `0029D210` + 0x33 with qword `0209C380`; then, when qword `0209C318` is non-null, it does the same with that qword (call at `0029D210` + 0x54, tail jump at `0029D210` + 0x65), otherwise it returns
takes the 0x38-byte record at `02EBD480` + (`ecx` AND 0x3F)*0x38 and, when its dword `+0x0` equals `ecx`, ORs 1 into its byte `+0x30`; otherwise it stores nothing

takes the 0x38-byte record at `02EBD480` + (`ecx` AND 0x3F)*0x38 and, when its dword `+0x0` equals `ecx` and its qword `+0x10` is non-null, writes that object's 16 bytes at `+0x320`: when bit 0x4000 of its word `+0x368` is set it stores 0x3F800000 to each of dwords `+0x320`, `+0x324`, `+0x328`, `+0x32C`, otherwise it copies 16 bytes from `rdx` to `+0x320` and then stores 0x3F800000 to dword `+0x32C`; a tag mismatch or null qword writes nothing

notes: 003B3AA0: 0x3F800000 is written as the raw immediate because the listing does not decode it as a float (it is the f32 bit pattern of 1.0). 0029D210: 00916330 is passed as an address only; the listing does not decode what it points to.
